_meta.indication: OZEMPIC is indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 3623 (SUSTAIN 1) - monotherapy vs placebo in drug-naive T2DM
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, multinational, multicenter, four-arm trial
pivotal_trials.population: Adult drug-naive patients with T2DM (HbA1c 7-10%) treated with diet and exercise
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to week 30 in HbA1c
pivotal_trials.result: HbA1c treatment difference vs placebo: Sema 0.5 mg -1.22% (95% CI -1.54, -0.90), p<.0001; Sema 1.0 mg -1.43% (95% CI -1.75, -1.11), p<.0001

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 3744 (SUSTAIN 6) - cardiovascular outcomes trial vs placebo
pivotal_trials.phase: Cardiovascular outcomes trial (short-duration CVOT to rule out excess CV risk pre-marketing)
pivotal_trials.design: Multi-national, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial to demonstrate non-inferiority for MACE, both added to standard-of-care
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with T2DM and high cardiovascular risk (>=50 years with clinical evidence of cardiovascular disease, or >=60 years with subclinical evidence)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time from randomization to first MACE (composite of CV death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke)
pivotal_trials.result: 254 first MACE; HR for MACE semaglutide vs placebo 0.74 (95% CI 0.58, 0.95), meeting non-inferiority. However, the secondary endpoint of diabetic retinopathy complications showed evidence of increased risk with semaglutide: HR 1.76 (95% CI 1.11, 2.78).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions are gastrointestinal: nausea (15.8% at 0.5 mg, 20.3% at 1 mg vs 6.1% placebo), vomiting (5.0%, 9.2% vs 2.3%), and diarrhea (8.5%, 8.8% vs 1.9%). Class safety concerns include pancreatitis, medullary thyroid tumors, and acute kidney injury.
target_moa: Semaglutide is a once-weekly glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist that binds to and activates the human GLP-1 receptor, increasing glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and lowering blood glucose and glucagon.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK OF THYROID C-CELL TUMORS. In rodents, semaglutide causes thyroid C-cell tumors; it is unknown whether OZEMPIC causes thyroid C-cell tumors, including medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), in humans. OZEMPIC is contraindicated in patients with a personal or family history of MTC or in patients with MEN 2.

rems.type: FDA determined that a REMS is not necessary for Ozempic (semaglutide) injection to ensure that its benefits outweigh its risks.

advisory_committee.vote: An Advisory Committee Meeting was held on October 18, 2017 to discuss the risks and benefits of semaglutide; all Advisory Committee members concluded that semaglutide was effective in improving glycemic control. No numeric vote tally is reported.

description.text: Added indication to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and established cardiovascular disease

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the addition of an indication to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction or non-fatal stroke) in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and established cardiovascular disease, and revised labeling to reflect the results of the SUSTAIN 6 cardiovascular outcomes trial, entitled, "A Long-term, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, Multinational, Multi-center Trial to Evaluate Cardiovascular and Other Long-term Outcomes With Semaglutide in Subjects With Type 2 Diabetes."

description.text: Added a 3rd maintenance dose of 2 mg subcutaneously once weekly

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for addition of a 3rd maintenance dose of Ozempic (2 mg subcutaneously once weekly) (2.68 mg/ml concentration).

description.text: Added new indication to reduce risk of sustained eGFR decline, end-stage kidney disease, and cardiovascular death in adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for a new indication to reduce the risk of sustained estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline, end-stage kidney disease, and cardiovascular death in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease.

basis.text: The application was reviewed under a standard (not priority) review designation.

summary.text: Semaglutide (Ozempic) NDA 209637 was submitted December 5, 2016 and reviewed under standard review with a PDUFA goal date of December 5, 2017. It was approved as a traditional (full) approval based on a phase 3 development program comprising five multinational efficacy trials plus one cardiovascular outcomes trial (SUSTAIN 6); of these, SUSTAIN 1 (efficacy) and SUSTAIN 6 (CVOT) are detailed among the pivotal_trials. An Advisory Committee meeting was held October 18, 2017.

citations.quote: Semaglutide phase 3 development program is comprised of 5 multi-national efficacy trials, one cardiovascular outcomes trial (CVOT) of short duration (not an efficacy trial – outcomes trial to rule out excessive CV risk pre-marketing)
An Advisory Committee Meeting was held to discuss the risks and benefits of semaglutide for subcutaneous injection on October 18, 2017.

requirement.text: 3294-1: Conduct a 26-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel group study of the safety and efficacy of Ozempic in pediatric patients ages 10 to 17 years, followed by a 26-week open-label controlled extension (deferred pediatric study under PREA).

citations.quote: 3294-1 Conduct a 26-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel group study of the safety and efficacy of Ozempic (semaglutide) for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus in pediatric patients ages 10 to 17 years (inclusive), followed by a 26-week open-label, controlled extension.

requirement.text: 3294-2: Conduct a medullary thyroid carcinoma registry-based case series of at least 15 years duration to systematically monitor the annual incidence of medullary thyroid carcinoma in the United States and identify any increase related to the introduction of Ozempic.

citations.quote: 3294-2 Conduct a medullary thyroid carcinoma registry-based case series of at least 15 years duration to systematically monitor the annual incidence of medullary thyroid carcinoma in the United States and to identify any increase related to the introduction of Ozempic (semaglutide) into the marketplace.

requirement.text: 3294-3: Develop and validate a sensitive assay to assess the neutralizing activity of anti-semaglutide antibodies and its cross-neutralizing effect on native GLP-1.

requirement.text: 3294-4: Conduct a study to assess the incidence of neutralizing antibodies to semaglutide and GLP-1 in subjects treated with semaglutide using the assays developed under PMC 3294-3.
